sources.title: Midjourney v6 is here — VentureBeat
sources.claim: Midjourney official v6 announcement: prompting differs significantly, users must relearn, v6 is much more sensitive.

sources.title: Midjourney v6 Guide — AI Tuts
sources.claim: Strip junk quality/camera words; be descriptive because v6 understands prompts much better.

sources.title: Midjourney v6 Reviewed — Gold Penguin
sources.claim: v6 takes long, complex, conversational prompts and fulfills nearly every element.

sources.title: Midjourney v6 In-Depth Review Part 2 — Midlibrary
sources.claim: Token-retention testing: v6 held all prompt elements through seven steps before dropping any.

sources.title: Midjourney V.6 Natural Language Focus — Medium
sources.claim: v6 shifts paradigm toward natural language: describe a scene rather than comma-separated keywords.

sources.title: Master Midjourney Word Art Prompts — ImaginePro
sources.claim: Text in double quotes is a literal instruction; --style raw gives more literal, less embellished result.

sources.title: Prompt Basics — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: Midjourney official docs: short simple prompts generate best images; seven elements to consider.

sources.title: Midjourney Prompt Guide 2026 — ImageToPrompt
sources.claim: Recommended v6 prompt order: subject, style/medium, lighting, color palette, composition, mood, parameters.

sources.title: Getting Started with Midjourney v6 — MLQ
sources.claim: v6 rewards explicit description, penalizes vague filler terms like 'award-winning', 'photorealistic', '4k/8k'.

sources.title: Midjourney v6 Prompt Structure
sources.claim: Six-component v6 recipe: style, subject, setting, composition, lighting, details.

sources.title: --stylize — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --stylize 0–1000 (default 100); low = literal, high = artistic freedom.

sources.title: --chaos — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --chaos 0–100 (default 0); higher = more different grid images.

sources.title: --weird — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --weird 0–3000 (default 0); experimental aesthetics; not fully compatible with seeds.

sources.title: --raw — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --style raw turns off auto-pilot styling; more realistic/literal results.

sources.title: Multi-Prompts & Weights — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --no X = X::-0.5; sum of all weights must stay positive.

sources.title: Legacy Features — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: v5-era default parameters: Quality 0.25/0.5/1, Stylize 0–1000 default 100, Chaos 0–100.

sources.title: --seed — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --seed 0–4294967295 for reproducibility; Turbo mode breaks reliable seed locking.

sources.title: --tile — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --tile generates seamless patterns; upscaling breaks the repeat.

sources.title: --quality — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --quality controls GPU time; only affects initial four-image set.

sources.title: Parameter List — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --ar sets aspect ratio (default 1:1); parameters go at end with no space before dashes.

sources.title: Midjourney Prompt Weights — AI Tuts
sources.claim: --no = ::-0.5 shorthand; negative weights are relative.

sources.title: Midjourney Image Weight — Aiarty
sources.claim: For v6 --iw accepts 0–3 (default 1), wider ceiling than 0–2 in earlier versions.

sources.title: Style Reference — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --sref URL/code + --sw 0–1000 (default 100); --sw 0 cancels the --sref.

sources.title: Deep Dive into Midjourney SREF Codes — Midlibrary
sources.claim: Sweet spot for --sw is 65–175; --sref random generates reusable numeric code.

sources.title: Character References — Midjourney Updates
sources.claim: --cref URL + --cw 0–100 (default 100); --cw 100 = face/hair/clothes, --cw 0 = face only.

sources.title: Mastering Midjourney v6 — JourneyAIArt
sources.claim: v6 is more sensitive to prompt wording; comma-keyword style that worked in earlier versions fails.

sources.title: --no parameter — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: --no is the dedicated way to exclude elements.

sources.title: Midjourney Negative Prompt — WhyTryAI
sources.claim: Writing 'without X' in positive prompt can emphasize the thing; --no X reliably removes it.

sources.title: Why Midjourney Prompts Don't Work — Prompt Architects
sources.claim: Stacking 5+ style modifiers causes them to average into mush.

sources.title: Midjourney v6 — Promptomania
sources.claim: Longer prompts make Midjourney assign weight 0.00 to important keywords, especially late ones.

sources.title: Midjourney v6 In-Depth Review Part 3 — Midlibrary
sources.claim: High --stylize lets Midjourney ignore specified details to polish the image.

sources.title: /shorten command — AI Tuts
sources.claim: /shorten scores each token 0–1 and strikes through near-zero-weight words.

sources.title: Using Underscores in Midjourney — Medium
sources.claim: Fusing words with underscores into single tokens raises per-token weight.

sources.title: Version History — Midjourney Docs
sources.claim: v6.1 default Jul 30 2024 – Jun 16 2025; v7 became default Jun 17 2025.

sources.title: V7 Alpha — Midjourney Updates
sources.claim: V7 is an entirely new model that may require different styles of prompting.

sources.title: Midjourney 2025 v7 Timeline — God of Prompt
sources.claim: V7 improved prompt understanding ~35%; simpler prompts now beat parameter-heavy approaches.

sources.title: Midjourney v7 Review 2026 — Evolink
sources.claim: V7 achieves precision through the model itself; V6 relied on parameter-heavy habits.

sources.title: SD vs Midjourney vs DALL-E 3 — ImageToPrompt
sources.claim: Prompting philosophies: MJ = aesthetic phrases+params, DALL-E 3 = natural prose, Flux = photographic terms, SD = weighted keywords.

sources.title: Midjourney vs Stable Diffusion vs Flux — PXZ
sources.claim: Flux follows instructions precisely; Midjourney is aesthetic-first and may ignore literal specs.

sources.title: 2026 AI Model Comparison — FreeAcademy
sources.claim: By 2026: Flux 2 launched Nov 2025, Midjourney v8 (native 2K) launched Mar 2026, GPT Image 2 replaced DALL-E 3.
